bug_semantics: CRI checkpoint restore (CreateContainer → CRImportCheckpoint) treats attacker-controlled checkpoint metadata as authoritative image identity. It reads RootfsImageRef/RootfsImageName from the checkpoint config.dump, pulls that ref, then ImageService.Create-tags the pulled content as RootfsImageName without verifying that the name matches the digest or that the caller is allowed to bind that local tag. A pod-create attacker can therefore inject a malicious image under an arbitrary NAME:TAG on the node; later pods using IfNotPresent/Never on the poisoned tag run the attacker image under the victim identity. ImageService.Create AlreadyExists is ignored, so a missing local tag is created; an existing NAME:TAG is not overwritten, but first-writer cache poisoning is enough.
flaw_origin: The retag-from-checkpoint-config sink was first written when CRI restore landed in 9e6beafd53919eecd1fb650a76332002cf4c84dd (PR #10365, Adrian Reber). Parent 07dd4ccf3599d4c22ee679b36fda3a17f8801cc2 only exported RootfsImageName/Ref into checkpoint metadata; it had no CRImportCheckpoint and no tagImage.Name assignment. cf7f4f5cc292fff86c5a920bbe2cb5abf62ff6bc later skipped pull when the digest was already cached but left the retag intact. The security fix deleted the Get/Create retag block.
